articles.title: Sam Darnold Exits Seahawks' Season Opener With Hip Injury
articles.description: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for the remainder of the team's season opener against the New England Patriots after suffering a right hip injury on the first drive on Wednesday night. Darnold landed on his right knee after being sacked from behind by former Seahawks linebacker Dre'Mont Jones on third down. He was examined in the medical tent before limping to the locker room as Seattle took the field for its second possession. Darnold was initially listed as questionable to return before being downgraded to out. Veteran backup Drew Lock entered in relief and completed 6 of his first 8 pass attempts for 51 yards. Seattle's offense struggled with penalties in the first half, committing four infractions, including an offside call that wiped out a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak attempt by tight end AJ Barner. That penalty came after Lock connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 21-yard gain on third-and-22. In a rematch of Seattle's Super Bowl LX win over New England, the Patriots took a 7-0 lead in the second quarter when Drake Maye found rookie tight end Eli Raridon for a 2-yard touchdown. New England had reached the goal line after Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe was flagged for pass interference on a flea-flicker. The Patriots extended their lead to 10-0 in the third quarter on a 50-yard field goal from Andy Borregales. Lock, 29, holds a 10-18 record as a starter across his first seven NFL seasons. He appeared in five games last season while Darnold started all 17 games for Seattle. Jalen Milroe was designated as Seattle's emergency third quarterback before the game, making him inactive but available to play if both Darnold and Lock were to exit with injury. The Seahawks went on to win the game 13-10 over the Patriots.

articles.title: Brock Bowers Out 1-2 Games With Meniscus Trim
articles.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is set to miss "a game or two" after undergoing a meniscus trim Tuesday, according to multiple reports. The procedure addressed an injury Bowers suffered during training camp, with the surgery having been scheduled last week. Bowers played through a PCL injury for much of last season, an issue that ultimately landed him on injured reserve for the final weeks of the year. His latest knee procedure marks a difficult start to the 2026 season and will complicate life for quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Raiders host the Miami Dolphins this weekend before traveling to face the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2. With Bowers sidelined, tight ends Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas are set to take on larger roles. The team's receiving corps also includes Tre Tucker, Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor, Dareke Young and sixth-round pick Malik Benson. Las Vegas does hope to have running back Ashton Jeanty available for Sunday's game. Jeanty returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since suffering an ankle injury on Aug. 23, and coach Klint Kubiak had expressed optimism last week that Jeanty would be ready for the start of the regular season.
